name: RS2
imitates: A small mayfly or midge emerger, especially baetis and midges; a staple tailwater pattern for fish rising to emergers.

steps.text: With the hook level in the vise, start the thread about a quarter shank length behind the eye and wrap forward a few turns to lock it.
Tie in two microfibbets about twice the hook shank in length and bind them down back to the start of the bend.
Split the tails by passing a short piece of thread around the bend between the two fibbets, then pulling it over the top of the shank.
Dub a slender noodle, make a wrap under the tails to lift them, then dub forward in touching turns to about two thirds of the shank.
Stack two or three CDC feathers with tips aligned and tie them in about half an inch behind the tips, tips pointing rearward.
Dub a fine noodle, make a turn or two behind the wing, then pass the dubbing in front of it to build a neat thorax, leaving a gap at the eye.
Whip finish behind the eye and trim the thread.
Separate the CDC from the tails, pull it upward, and snip it at roughly a 45 degree angle to the shank. The finished fly.
